items.title: What happens to your pets when you die?
items.summary: Without a proper plan – whether in a trust or will – your beloved companion could face an animal shelter or worse The idea of making a will may be uncomfortable, but routine. Ensuring that your family and estate is taken care of is a kindness. But there’s one thing clients often aren’t sure how to handle, says Azriel J Baer, a trust and estate attorney at New York-based law firm Farrell Fritz, PC: what will happen to their pet . items.imageAlt: What happens to your pets when you die?

items.title: Say a little prayer for the guests to leave | Brief letters
items.summary: Pass the rosary beads | Let the cat out | Turn on the TV | Show the holiday slides | Passive-aggressive wit | Tea before you go? Trying to get guests to go home ( Letters, 6 October )? No problem in lots of Irish homes years ago. Simply start to frantically search for spare rosary beads, expressing the number of visitors you need them for, and then start moving chairs around in preparation for the rosary. Usually worked. items.summary: Council car parks have switched away from ticket machines to cut costs, leading to extra fees for users Drivers are unwittingly paying up to 40% more to park as more councils switch to app-only payments and force customers to pick up the tab. Many councils across England have removed pay and display machines and replaced them with app payments, including a number in London. items.title: A lakeside idyll: laid-back cycling and autumn hikes on Italy’s Lake Iseo
items.summary: Smaller and less visited than Como and Garda, Lake Iseo harbours a gorgeous car-free island ideal for easy-going cycling and sightseeing Rust red and burnt sienna speckle the green mountain rising from Lake Iseo. Monte Isola, Italy’s largest lake island, is a peak of sheer cliffs and dense forest, dotted with old fishing hamlets and hillside villages, each as pretty as the terraced villas of Lake Como and Garda, but with far fewer visitor s . items.title: Henry Harris’ recipe for tarte Vaudoise à la creme
items.summary: This fantastic tart is a minor miracle invented by a legendary chef, yet it has very few ingredients and an intriguing technique for baking it Often, the greatest dishes are made from very few ingredients and with pretty standard techniques, and this tart is one of them. It’s based on an old Frédy Girardet recipe that, despite his reputation as one of the all-time greats, calls only for a simple application of process to deliver a knockout result (which is one reason I put it in my latest book). A pastry case is spread with sugar and cream, then dotted with butter and sprinkled with cinnamon.
